title: Block Parameters
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of block parameters in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply block parameters in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to destructuring values and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Block Parameters through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding block parameters helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Block Parameters helps you reason about parameter syntax. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Parameter syntax. Then connect it to Multiple block arguments. The remaining syllabus points—Destructuring values—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Block Parameters
content_blocks.code:
def around
  puts "start"
  yield
  puts "finish"
end
around { puts "work" }

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.title: Mixing too many concerns
items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports block parameters. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for block parameters using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Destructuring values), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain block parameters, identify its place in blocks, procs, lambdas, and closures, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
